setupTitle.message: Two things and you are set up

setupLead.message: After this, ⌘S on a document you opened by double-clicking writes straight back to the file — no destination prompt, ever.

setupStep1Note.message: One broad folder is usually enough — it covers everything inside it. Chrome will not hand over your home folder itself, or Library: choose Documents, Desktop, or the folder your documents live in.

setupUpgradeNote.message: Upgrading and expected your folders to be here? An unpacked extension is identified by its folder path, so loading a new copy from a different folder makes it a different extension. Your folders are still granted to the old one. Replace the files in the original folder and press Reload in chrome://extensions instead.

helpWhatSub.message: A Bento document is one HTML file that carries its own editor. Opened straight from disk, a browser will not let it write back to itself — so saving asks you where to put it, every time. bento/home is what removes that question.

tourSaveBody.message: ⌘S writes straight back to the file you opened, with no dialog. Autosave and in-place updates go the same way.

tourFindBody.message: Every Bento document in your folders, with its real title and a picture of its first page. Search covers what is written inside them.

tourSwitchBody.message: Press <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>B</kbd>, or right-click inside a document, for a panel beside it.

tourNewBody.message: + New document fetches the current release of Slides, Spaces or Dash and puts a fresh document in your folder.

helpNeedsSub.message: Two things, both outside this extension’s power to arrange.

helpFolderGranted.message: $1 granted — documents inside them save in place

helpFolderNone.message: Not chosen yet. One broad folder covers everything inside it.

helpAccessOff.message: Off. Turn on Allow access to file URLs in chrome://extensions — no extension can turn this on for itself.
helpAccessOff.description: REVIEW: explains a browser permission — a mistranslation costs the user their setup.

helpAccessUnknown.description: REVIEW: explains a browser permission — a mistranslation costs the user their setup.

helpAccessOn.description: REVIEW: explains a browser permission — a mistranslation costs the user their setup.

helpNeverSub.message: It reads and writes only inside the folders above, and only the file a page was actually opened from — the browser tells it which, so a document cannot name somebody else’s file. Nothing about your documents is uploaded anywhere, and the extension has no server to upload them to.
